question: Will the IOM Missing Migrants Project record at least 900 Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026 before April 2026?
summary: Baseline ensemble is 68%, and no formal forecast supports a precise 900-death threshold by end-March; February tally around 606 suggests a March spike would be unusual.
Objections identify weather-driven risk as a potential upward pressure, but also emphasize the lack of concrete forecasts predicting such a spike, introducing substantial uncertainty.
Threshold arithmetic indicates reaching 900 by end-March would require an unusually high March death toll (around 294), which is historically unlikely, though not literally impossible.
Overall calibration favors preserving the ensemble estimate with a modestly wider, uncertainty-aware range to reflect volatile conditions and incomplete forecast information.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections highlight plausible near-term risks (weather, volatility) and lack of a forecast, but do not reveal a systematic error in the ensemble; the threshold remains unlikely but not ruled out.
